newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada braced for economic boom, brokerage says.
newsitem.headline: Canada braced for economic boom, brokerage says.

text.p: Canada has entered a boom period of strong economic growth, higher consumer confidence and declining unemployment, said a forecast released on Thursday by a Canadian brokerage.
The Nesbitt Burns quarterly forecast said the Canadian economy was braced for a powerful growth phase unseen since the boom years of the 1980s.
"We expect real GDP to expand 4.0 percent this year and at least 3.5 percent next year," said Sherry Cooper, chief economist with Nesbitt Burns.
"Over the longer term, look for rising stock prices, falling interest rates and a long and sustained expansion," Cooper added.
The forecast also predicted Canada's unemployment rate, currently 9.1 percent, would drop below 9 percent by the end of 1997 and below 8 percent by the end of 1998.
Cooper estimated the employment spurt would lead to the creation of about 500,000 jobs.
Surging personal and corporate income tax revenues would practically eliminate the federal deficit for fiscal 1997-98 ending March 31, the forecast said.
